newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks non-commital on plans to buy Mack.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks non-commital on plans to buy Mack.

text.p: Volvo Trucks, a unit of Sweden's Volvo, would neither confirm nor deny a Tuesday newspaper report that it planned to buy French vehicle maker Renault's U.S. truck group Mack.
"We don't plan any other cooperation than the discussions we are having with Mitsubishi," Volvo Trucks' spokesman Kjell Drotz told Reuters.
When asked if an acquisition of Mack could be seen as something other than cooperation, he said: "That is not the way you should interpret it."
Drotz admitted, however, that Volvo Trucks is looking at different strategies and scenarios.

Daily Svenska Dagbladet reported on Tuesday that Volvo Trucks planned to buy Mack to meet its target of a 20 percent U.S. market share. Currently, Volvo Trucks has a 10 percent market share and Mack 8.8 percent.
"The deal would double Volvo's market share and give it access to Mack's network of retailers and service plants in the U.S.," the newspaper said.
But the newspaper said the deal had complications. Renault would think of selling Mack -- but Volvo would also have to take over Renault's previously troubled European truck operations.
Svenska Dagbladet said Volvo was not interested in doing that.
